mechanism: Coding agents choose and provision infrastructure, so the agent is the buyer in practice. Defaults, documentation quality and MCP support decide which vendor gets picked.
winners: Backends agents reach for by default: Supabase, Neon, Vercel, Stripe, GitHub, Cloudflare. Agent vendors themselves.
exposed: Tools that can only be set up through a GUI, seat-priced developer software, vendors absent from agent defaults.
main_risk: Dependence on one or two coding agents, and revenue from throwaway projects.

mechanism: Agents and crawlers read content without sending a visit. Search referrals fall and revenue has to move to licensing, pay-per-crawl and direct audiences.
winners: Toll collectors at the network edge, publishers with loyal direct readers, owners of unique data.
exposed: Small publishers that depend on search.
main_risk: Pay-per-crawl revenue is undisclosed, and blocking crawlers has cost traffic.

mechanism: Assistants become the discovery and comparison layer and send pre-qualified traffic. Checkout still mostly completes on the merchant's own site, and the contest is over catalog access and who owns the customer.
winners: Catalog platforms, merchants with clean structured data, large retailers running their own agent inside assistants, card networks.
exposed: Marketplaces that live on sponsored listings, thin affiliates, merchants whose product pages agents cannot read.
main_risk: Checkout inside chat underperforming, losing the customer relationship, and platforms blocking agents.

mechanism: Answers replace lists of links. Budgets move to placements beside AI answers and to optimisation for models. When an agent picks the product, persuasion targets the model and the product feed.
winners: Google, GEO platforms, brands that third parties cite often.
exposed: Classic SEO and affiliate arbitrage, and retail media if agents skip sponsored listings.
main_risk: Opaque measurement, and chatbot ad revenue running well below OpenAI's targets.

mechanism: Card networks add agent tokens, mandates and registries. Stablecoin rails target machine micropayments. In banking, agents that move deposits and shop for rates attack profits built on customer inertia.
winners: Card networks, Stripe and Adyen, tokenisation providers, stablecoin infrastructure, fraud vendors.
exposed: Banks that rely on low-rate deposits and issuers slow to support agent tokens.
main_risk: Liability is unallocated and crypto rails carry a lot of artificial volume.

mechanism: AI is a major planning surface already. Booking is being wired in through apps and hotel partners, but travellers hesitate to hand over the transaction.
winners: Online travel agencies and chains with inventory APIs inside assistants.
exposed: Metasearch and content-led travel sites, properties without machine-readable rates.
main_risk: High cost of an error on an expensive booking, and loyalty lock-in.

mechanism: Vertical agents do associate-level work, which moves pricing pressure from hours to outcomes.
winners: Vertical AI vendors and firms that reprice to outcomes.
exposed: Firms whose model is billing junior hours.
main_risk: Liability for agent output. The figures here rest on single sources.

mechanism: Agents quote, book, schedule and track freight. Shipper and carrier agents begin to transact with each other.
winners: Data-rich brokers and third-party logistics firms.
main_risk: Only vendor-reported best cases exist, with no independent data.

impact_expected: 2027 at the edge, 2029 to 2030 for access networks
mechanism: Agent traffic changes the volume and shape of network load and creates demand for edge inference, bot classification and identity at the network layer.
winners: Edge and CDN platforms, network equipment vendors.
exposed: Operators that carry the traffic without charging for it.

mechanism: Agents run the front and back office, the article's self-running small business. Use today is mostly individual productivity.
winners: Platforms that bundle agents for small firms, niche merchants agents can discover.
exposed: Small firms agents cannot see, local lead-generation intermediaries.
main_risk: Privacy and security worries, a skills gap and unproven returns.

mechanism: Buyer-side agents source, compare and reorder. Sellers need machine-readable catalogs, prices and terms. Coding agents buying developer infrastructure is the one live example.
winners: Distributors with API-first catalogs, procurement suites, B2B payment and credit rails.
exposed: Distributors that sell on relationships alone and vendors with opaque pricing.
main_risk: ERP integration and whether an agent has authority to sign a contract.

mechanism: Agents take on patient access, scheduling and back-office work. Consumer agents begin to touch provider sites. Regulated data slows autonomy.
winners: Voice and scheduling agent vendors, providers with open scheduling APIs.
main_risk: Liability, privacy law and high-risk classification in the EU.
